instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Exactly Within Policy
cards.instruction: Agree to every request only after interpreting the policy so it grants you authority, protection, or an exemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The volunteer policy puts seniors in supervision, so yes, I'll help clean the hall. I taught you to mop from the far corner; I'll check your progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking you to mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Supervision covers mopping. On that basis, gladly. You chose the right tool this time; start at the far end and I'll direct.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who's actually holding it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The policy leaves practical work to trainees. You can hold it, and I'll accept responsibility for showing you the corner you always miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our shared-effort rule counts hosting, so yes, I'll host Christmas. You can roast the potatoes; I taught you that before you could reach the top shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What are you cooking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hosting is my share under the rule. I'll gladly oversee yours. You've got the potatoes crisp at last; don't crowd the tray now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You won't even chop the carrots?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Teaching counts as effort too, so yes, I'll stand beside you and supervise the chopping. Use the grip I showed you.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: New Rule Required
cards.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spilled the tea. From now on, pouring needs a permit. I taught you to steady the pot; you can show me that before you get one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who signs it? My bus leaves in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll appoint a pouring supervisor. Good, you're checking who's responsible now. Nobody pours until they've watched your grip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our last supervisor spilled a whole jug himself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then supervisors need a second signature before they pour. Write that down; you've brought me a problem worth adding to the checklist at last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone blinked in the family photo. Draw up a blinking rota before we try again. I taught you to count people in, not hope their eyes cooperate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't schedule a blink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful objection, for once. We'll rehearse unscheduled blinking before each picture. You can lead the count the way we practised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Grandma's taxi comes in ten minutes. That rehearsal will take all afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then appoint a timekeeper to approve its length. You used to let rehearsals drift; put Grandma in charge of the clock before we begin.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Lend Me the Edge
cards.instruction: Get someone to provide the one advantage you need without making the eventual success feel borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lend me your good racket for the final. I taught you that backhand; I'd like to play mine on strings that haven't sagged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you admit my racket helped?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll thank the strings. The strokes are mine. You've become quite particular about equipment since I stopped lending you everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use your own, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Its loose strings would take the blame if I lost. Give me yours so we can see my actual backhand. You know the stroke; I taught it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What temperature won you the cake prize? Just the setting; I'm not taking on a co-baker. I taught you the sponge, and this recipe is mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do you want my secret recipe as well?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it. You measured properly at last, and I only need the number on the dial. I'll do the baking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That temperature is most of the trick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then whisper it while I set the oven. You can check I've copied the number, the way I checked yours; the entry still goes under my name.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Stay for the Result
cards.instruction: Keep them present until the contest, bargain, or consequence reaches an undeniable outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay at the allotment until we've weighed both pumpkins. I taught you to record a crop properly; you don't leave a result to a glance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is clearly bigger.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A better eye than you had when we started. Now stay to see how much bigger. Read the scale with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tell me tomorrow. I need to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow you'll question the scale. Read this number now, the way I showed you, and write it beside yours. Then you can go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, read the final dinner bill with me. I taught you to check the total before walking away from the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can split it later.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're quicker at offering a split now. First find the line for that 'just a starter' you ordered. Read the price aloud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay my share. I don't need a lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me you can total those lines without me. Stay until we both have the same number; you can transfer it later.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Admit It Wasn’t Fair
cards.instruction: Get an apology that acknowledges how the rules, comparison, or outcome worked against you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologise for starting me behind the shed before you congratulate the winner. I taught you to line up runners where they can see the course.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still finished last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You read the results correctly, at least. I spent ten seconds finding the race. Start your apology there, not at the finish line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was an honest mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep 'mistake', then say, 'I gave you a worse start than everyone else.' Don't ask me to mark you on good intentions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologise for announcing I baked the cake before judging. I taught you to present numbered plates so nobody started with a favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost on flavour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said 'another interesting attempt' before anyone tasted it. Clear diction, at least; now apologise for telling them what to expect.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was encouraging you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for encouraging the judges to doubt my cake before they tasted it. That isn't the neutral introduction I taught you.
